youtube.title: The #1 Wealth Killer No One Talks About: Lifestyle Creep
youtube.description:
Lifestyle creep is the quiet wealth killer: every raise you get disappears into slightly nicer everything, and your savings never move. Here's how lifestyle creep works, what it really costs, the warning signs, and a simple 50/50 raise rule to beat it without giving up the things you enjoy.

Chapters
0:00 Intro
0:17 What it is
0:47 The raise that vanishes
1:25 Not just low incomes
2:05 The whole country
2:22 Why it happens
3:02 The real cost
3:35 Warning signs
4:00 The fix
5:12 Recap

Numbers in this video
• Adults with 3 months of expenses set aside, by family income: 21% (under $25K), 39% ($25K–$50K), 55% ($50K–$100K), 75% ($100K+). 55% of all adults. (Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025, published May 2026)
• U.S. personal saving rate: 4.1% of disposable income in October 2026 (Bureau of Economic Analysis, Personal Income and Outlays, released Nov 25, 2026)
• Sam is a made-up example: a $5,000 raise on $60,000 is roughly $300 a month after tax; your take-home depends on your taxes.
• Growth examples assume a 7% yearly return, compounded monthly, for 30 years: $300/month grows to about $366,000 (you put in $108,000); $150/month to about $183,000. Illustrations only, not guaranteed.
